data.name: Mara
data.gender_notes: Mara is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Mara was a goddess of the sea. In the Bible, Mara was the name of a bitter spring that the Israelites complained about in the wilderness. This name may symbolize one who is rebellious or bitter, but ultimately overcomes adversity. The name Mara carries the meaning “Rebellious, bitter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Mara usually hope their child will grow to embody rebellious, bitter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mara belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rebellious, bitter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mara total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_latin.name: Mara

in_english.name: Mara
in_english.long_meaning: Mara is a name derived from Hebrew roots, meaning bitter woman or sorrowful one, and is associated with the biblical figure of Mara, a woman who experienced a life of hardship and sorrow, yet remained steadfast in her faith

data.cultural_impact: Mara has been used as a given name in various cultures throughout history, including the Maronites in Lebanon, who trace their origins to ancient Phoenicia. The name may also have roots in Hebrew, meaning "bitter" or "rebellious," which reflects the experiences of the Israelites in the desert as recorded in the Book of Exodus.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Mara holds a deeper spiritual meaning as a reminder of God's faithfulness and provision, even in the midst of hardships and bitterness. The Israelites, despite their complaints, were led to a place of abundance and sustenance, as God guided them through the desert and provided them with water from the rock. Mara, then, can serve as a reminder to trust in God's guidance and to rely on His promises, even when we are facing trials and bitter experiences.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mara, in Hebrew, means "bitter" or " rebellious." In the Christian context, it symbolizes the struggle against temptation and the bitterness of sin. The name evokes the challenge of overcoming internal and external adversities, reminding us of the transformative power of faith and redemption.

biblical_reference.note: Mara is the name given to Naomi after her husband and sons died

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mara was an early Christian martyr in North Africa. The name Mara carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mara was a Berber woman who was martyred during the Roman persecution of Christians in North Africa. She is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church.
